questions.question: Find the smallest number to be added to 999, so that 99 divides the sum exactly.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide the given number 999 by the divisor 99 to find the remainder.

999 ÷ 99 = 10 with a remainder of 9.

The smallest number to add = Divisor − Remainder.

Required number = 99 − 9 = 90.

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 999

Divisor = 99

**Formula Used:**

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

Number to be added = Divisor − Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, divide 999 by 99 to identify the quotient and the remainder.

⇒ 999 = (99 × 10) + 9

⇒ Thus, the remainder is 9.

⇒ To make the given number perfectly divisible, we must add the difference between the divisor and the remainder.

⇒ Number to be added = Divisor − Remainder

⇒ Number to be added = 99 − 9 = 90

⇒ Alternatively, the next multiple of 99 greater than 999 is 99 × 11 = 1089.

⇒ Required addition = 1089 − 999 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule for Addition

When a number N is divided by a divisor D giving a remainder R, the smallest number to be added to N to make it completely divisible by D is (D − R).

Rule for Subtraction

When a number N is divided by a divisor D giving a remainder R, the smallest number to be subtracted from N to make it completely divisible by D is exactly the remainder R itself.

Divisibility Rule of 99

A number is exactly divisible by 99 if it is completely divisible by both 9 (the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9) and 11 (the difference of alternating sums of its digits is 0 or a multiple of 11).
</p

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 2√10, where x > 1, then the value of (x³ - 1/x³) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = p, then x − 1/x = √(p² − 4).

Given p = 2√10, so x − 1/x = √(40 − 4) = √36 = 6.

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

Substituting k = 6:

x³ − 1/x³ = 6³ + 3 × 6 = 216 + 18 = 234.

**∴ The correct answer is 234.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 1/x = 2√10, where x > 1

**Formula Used:**

(x − 1/x)² = (x + 1/x)² − 4

x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)³ + 3(x − 1/x)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = (2√10)² − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 4 × 10 − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 40 − 4 = 36

⇒ Since x > 1, x − 1/x will be positive. So, x − 1/x = √36 = 6

⇒ Now, substitute this into the cube formula:

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (6)³ + 3 × 6

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 216 + 18

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 234

**∴ The correct answer is 234.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Rule

If x + 1/x = a, then x² + 1/x² = a² − 2.

Cube Rule (Plus)

If x + 1/x = a, then x³ + 1/x³ = a³ − 3a.

Sign Conversion Rule

If x + 1/x = a, then x − 1/x = √(a² − 4). Similarly, if x − 1/x = a, then x + 1/x = √(a² + 4).
</p

questions.question: In an election between two candidates P and Q, P got 78% of the total valid votes. If the total votes of the electorate were 75,60,000, then what was the number of valid votes that Q got if 10% of the voters did not cast their vote and 15% of the votes polled were declared invalid?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Valid votes received by Q can be directly found using successive percentage multipliers.

Q's Valid Votes = Total Electorate × Polled % × Valid % × Q's Share %

⇒ Q's Valid Votes = 75,60,000 × 90% × 85% × (100% − 78%)

⇒ Q's Valid Votes = 75,60,000 × (9 ÷ 10) × (17 ÷ 20) × (11 ÷ 50)

⇒ Q's Valid Votes = 7560 × 9 × 17 × 11 = 12,72,348

**∴ The correct answer is 12,72,348.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b1650c0845c2b60993cb48dc3569602c70932596bbe7892f3d020e976721f31.png] 

**Given:**

Total votes of the electorate = 75,60,000

Percentage of voters who did not vote = 10%

Percentage of invalid votes = 15%

Percentage of valid votes secured by P = 78%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of votes polled = (100% − 10%) of 75,60,000

⇒ Number of votes polled = 90% of 75,60,000 = (90 ÷ 100) × 75,60,000 = 68,04,000

⇒ Number of valid votes = (100% − 15%) of 68,04,000

⇒ Number of valid votes = 85% of 68,04,000 = (85 ÷ 100) × 68,04,000 = 57,83,400

⇒ Since P got 78% of the valid votes, Q must have received the remaining valid votes.

⇒ Percentage of valid votes Q received = 100% − 78% = 22%

⇒ Number of valid votes Q got = 22% of 57,83,400

⇒ Number of valid votes Q got = (22 ÷ 100) × 57,83,400 = 12,72,348

**∴ The correct answer is 12,72,348.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Method

When a base value continuously undergoes percentage reductions or increments sequentially, the final value can be obtained via a single chain product: Base × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100).

Election Base Shifting

It is crucial to remember that the percentage of invalid votes is calculated strictly on the 'Polled Votes', not on the 'Total Electorate'. The base automatically changes after every reduction in real-time election distribution problems.
</p

questions.question: In a circle, two chords MN and PQ intersect at O. If MO = 9 cm, ON = 5 cm and OQ = 6 cm, then the value of OP (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Intersecting Chords Theorem, the product of the segments of each intersecting chord is equal.

MO × ON = OP × OQ

9 × 5 = OP × 6

OP = 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two chords MN and PQ intersect at point O inside the circle.

Length of segment MO = 9 cm

Length of segment ON = 5 cm

Length of segment OQ = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Intersecting Chords Theorem: When two chords intersect inside a circle, the product of their respective segments is equal.

⇒ MO × ON = OP × OQ

**Calculations:**

⇒ 9 × 5 = OP × 6

⇒ 45 = 6 × OP

⇒ OP = 45 ÷ 6

⇒ OP = 15 ÷ 2

⇒ OP = 7.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intersecting Secants Theorem

If two secants are drawn to a circle from one exterior point P, the product of the external segment and the total secant length is equal for both secants (PA × PB = PC × PD).

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent and a secant meet at an exterior point P, the square of the tangent length is equal to the product of the secant's external segment and its total length (PT² = PA × PB).

Perpendicular from Center

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.
</p

questions.question: In a △ABC right-angled at C, if tan A = √3, then the value of sin A cos B cot(A + B) is:
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ In a right-angled △ABC right-angled at C, the total sum of angles is 180°. Since ∠C = 90°, the sum of the remaining two angles must be A + B = 90°. We are required to find the value of the expression sin A × cos B × cot(A + B). By substituting A + B = 90° into the expression, we get cot(90°), which equals 0. Because any finite value multiplied by 0 results in 0, the entire expression evaluates to 0 without needing to find tan A. **∴ The correct answer is 0.**

questions.question: A rectangular courtyard is 4m 95cm long and 16m 65cm broad. It is to be paved with the square tiles of the same size. Find the least number of such square tiles required to pave the rectangular courtyard.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert dimensions into the same unit: Length = 495 cm, Breadth = 1665 cm.

For the least number of tiles, the size of the square tile must be maximum.

Maximum side of the square tile = HCF(495, 1665) = 45 cm.

Least number of tiles = (Area of Courtyard) ÷ (Area of One Tile).

Least number of tiles = (495 × 1665) ÷ (45 × 45) = 11 × 37 = 407.

**∴ The correct answer is 407 tiles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of courtyard (L) = 4 m 95 cm = 495 cm

Breadth of courtyard (B) = 16 m 65 cm = 1665 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of square tile = Side²

Total number of tiles = Area of the rectangle ÷ Area of the square tile

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60f5b3e82cb93ec1f7321408651b339e13c584ee00035ff76952673881ca0169.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ To minimize the number of square tiles, we need the largest possible tile size.

⇒ The size of the largest square tile is the highest common factor (HCF) of the length and breadth.

⇒ Prime factorization of 495 = 3 × 3 × 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 1665 = 3 × 3 × 5 × 37

⇒ HCF(495, 1665) = 3 × 3 × 5 = 45 cm

⇒ So, the side of each identical square tile = 45 cm

⇒ Number of tiles required = (L × B) ÷ (Side × Side)

⇒ Number of tiles required = (495 × 1665) ÷ (45 × 45)

⇒ Number of tiles required = (495 ÷ 45) × (1665 ÷ 45)

⇒ Number of tiles required = 11 × 37 = 407

**∴ The correct answer is 407 tiles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Application of HCF in Mensuration

When asked to find the largest identical square shape that perfectly fits inside a rectangle without leaving gaps, always calculate the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the dimensions.

Least Number of Tiles Rule

To minimize the number of tiles required to completely fill an area, the size of each tile must be maximized. Number of tiles = (Total Area) ÷ (HCF × HCF).

Conversion of Units

Remember that 1 meter (m) = 100 centimeters (cm). Always ensure all measurements are brought into a common single unit prior to finding the HCF or computing the area.
</p

questions.question: A circular track's inner and outer radii are 25 m and 28 m respectively. The cost (in ₹) of levelling the track at ₹28 per m² is: [Use π = 22/7]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost = Area of Track × Rate per m²

Total Cost = π(R² − r²) × Rate

Total Cost = (22/7) × (28² − 25²) × 28

Total Cost = 22 × (28 − 25) × (28 + 25) × 4

Total Cost = 22 × 3 × 53 × 4 = 13992

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,992.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer radius (R) = 28 m

Inner radius (r) = 25 m

Rate of levelling = ₹28 per m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of circular track = π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92ef3b348fdf77e39ab4f01433427d41fa84fcf6e8f8d5f688431c7c8b11cf1d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (22/7) × (28² − 25²)

⇒ Area = (22/7) × (28 − 25) × (28 + 25)

⇒ Area = (22/7) × 3 × 53

⇒ Area = 3498/7 m²

⇒ Total Cost = Area × Rate

⇒ Total Cost = (3498/7) × 28

⇒ Total Cost = 3498 × 4

⇒ Total Cost = 13992

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,992.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circular Ring

The region bounded by two concentric circles is called a circular ring or track. Area = π(R² − r²) = π(R − r)(R + r).

Difference Between Fencing and Levelling

Fencing relates to the boundary, so Cost of Fencing = Perimeter × Rate per unit length. Levelling refers to making the surface flat, so Cost of Levelling = Area × Rate per unit area.

Perimeter of a Semicircle

The total perimeter includes the curved arc and the straight diameter. Perimeter = πr + 2r = r(π + 2).

questions.question: There are two pipes to fill a tank. Together, they can fill the tank in 15 minutes. If one pipe can fill the tank in one and a half times as fast as the other, the faster pipe alone can fill the tank in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of efficiency of faster pipe to slower pipe = 1.5 : 1 = 3 : 2.

Total combined efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min.

Total capacity of tank = Combined efficiency × Time = 5 × 15 = 75 units.

Time required by faster pipe alone = Total capacity ÷ Faster pipe efficiency = 75 ÷ 3 = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by both pipes together = 15 minutes.

Faster pipe fills 1.5 times as fast as the slower pipe.

**Method Used:**

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Time Taken

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Faster Pipe
 25
 75
 3
 
 

 Slower Pipe
 37.5
 2
 
 

 Both Pipes
 15
 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the slower pipe be 2 units/min.

⇒ Efficiency of the faster pipe = 1.5 × 2 = 3 units/min.

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min.

⇒ Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Combined Time

⇒ Total Work = 5 × 15 = 75 units.

⇒ Time required by faster pipe = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of faster pipe

⇒ Time = 75 ÷ 3 = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, its efficiency (part filled in 1 hour) is 1/x. For an outlet pipe emptying the tank in y hours, its efficiency is −1/y.

Efficiency & Time Relationship

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to the efficiency. Ratio of Time = 1 ÷ Ratio of Efficiency.

Combined Work Formula

When two pipes working together take times A and B respectively, their combined time T is given by T = (A × B) ÷ (A + B).
</p

questions.question:
Find the value of

frac{sec 35circ}{cosec 55circ} - frac{cos 25circ}{sin 65circ}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the complementary angle properties: sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Therefore, sec 35° = cosec 55° and cos 25° = sin 65°.

The expression becomes: (cosec 55° / cosec 55°) − (sin 65° / sin 65°)

⇒ 1 − 1 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(sec 35° / cosec 55°) − (cos 25° / sin 65°)

**Formula Used:**

sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ

cos(90° − θ) = sin θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ sec 35° = sec(90° − 55°) = cosec 55°

⇒ cos 25° = cos(90° − 65°) = sin 65°

Substituting these values into the given expression:

⇒ (cosec 55° / cosec 55°) − (sin 65° / sin 65°)

⇒ 1 − 1

⇒ 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles in Trigonometry

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

sin θ = 1 / cosec θ, cos θ = 1 / sec θ, and tan θ = 1 / cot θ.
</p

questions.question: If the perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 36 units, then its area is (in square units):
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the equilateral triangle = Perimeter ÷ 3 = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 units.

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × (side)²

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 144 = 36√3 square units.

**∴ The correct answer is 36√3 square units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ba0ba256c6c5775cf9b507fc067924fee8169c0272afa86dcb6f862857ae72c.png] 

**Given:**

Perimeter of the equilateral triangle = 36 units

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of an equilateral triangle = 3 × a (where 'a' is the side length)

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 × a = 36

⇒ a = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 units

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 12²

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 144

⇒ Area = 36√3 square units

**∴ The correct answer is 36√3 square units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Altitude of an Equilateral Triangle

The height (or altitude) of an equilateral triangle is given by h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a, where 'a' is the length of the side.

Inradius and Circumradius

For an equilateral triangle, Inradius (r) = a ÷ (2√3) and Circumradius (R) = a ÷ √3. The ratio of the circumradius to the inradius is always 2:1.

Area of an Isosceles Triangle

Area = (b ÷ 4) × √(4a² − b²), where 'a' is the length of the two equal sides and 'b' is the base.
</p

questions.question: If a sin³X + b cos³X = sinX cosX and a sinX = b cosX, then find the value of a² + b², provided that x is neither 0° nor 90°.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put X = 45° (valid as X is not 0° or 90°). From a sinX = b cosX ⇒ a(1/√2) = b(1/√2) ⇒ a = b.

Substitute in first equation: a(1/√2)³ + a(1/√2)³ = (1/√2) × (1/√2).

⇒ 2a / (2√2) = 1/2 ⇒ a/√2 = 1/2 ⇒ a = 1/√2. Thus, b = 1/√2.

Required value = a² + b² = (1/√2)² + (1/√2)² = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a sin³X + b cos³X = sinX cosX

a sinX = b cosX

**Formula Used:**

sin²X + cos²X = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the first expression, rewrite b cos³X as (b cosX) × cos²X

⇒ a sin³X + (b cosX) × cos²X = sinX cosX

⇒ Substitute b cosX = a sinX into the above equation:

⇒ a sin³X + (a sinX) × cos²X = sinX cosX

⇒ Take out the common term a sinX:

⇒ a sinX × (sin²X + cos²X) = sinX cosX

⇒ Using the formula sin²X + cos²X = 1:

⇒ a sinX × 1 = sinX cosX

⇒ Since X ≠ 0°, sinX ≠ 0, so dividing both sides by sinX gives:

⇒ a = cosX

⇒ Now substitute a = cosX into the second given equation a sinX = b cosX:

⇒ cosX × sinX = b cosX

⇒ Since X ≠ 90°, cosX ≠ 0, so dividing both sides by cosX gives:

⇒ b = sinX

⇒ Now calculate the required value a² + b²:

⇒ a² + b² = cos²X + sin²X

⇒ a² + b² = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

There are three primary Pythagorean identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Value Putting Strategy

When options are absolute constants (independent of variables), replacing variables with valid standard angles (like 30°, 45°, or 60°) quickly yields the answer without complex algebra. Always avoid angles causing division by zero or infinity.

Domain Constraints in Simplification

The question explicitly states X is neither 0° nor 90° because sin(0°) = 0 and cos(90°) = 0, which would lead to an invalid elimination of variables when simplifying equations by cancellation.
</p

questions.question: A dishonest merchant sells his grocery using weights that are 12% less than the true weights and makes a profit of 10%. Find his total gain percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for dishonest dealer total gain %: [ (Profit % + Less Weight %) ÷ (100 − Less Weight %) ] × 100

Given, Profit % = 10% and Less Weight % = 12%.

⇒ Total Gain % = [ (10 + 12) ÷ (100 − 12) ] × 100

⇒ Total Gain % = (22 ÷ 88) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

questions.question: Atul gives Vishu a head-start of 20 seconds in a 900 m race and beats him by 135 m. While running the same race again Atul gives a start of 189 m and beats him by 8 seconds. In how much time can Vishu complete the full race of 900 m?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Atul finish the race in T seconds. Vishu covers (900 − 135) = 765 m in (T + 20) seconds.

In the second case, Vishu covers (900 − 189) = 711 m in (T + 8) seconds.

Difference in distance for Vishu = 765 − 711 = 54 m, and difference in time = 20 − 8 = 12 seconds.

Vishu's speed = 54 ÷ 12 = 4.5 m/s.

Time taken by Vishu to cover 900 m = 900 ÷ 4.5 = 200 seconds = 3 minutes 20 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb35843600fd484f83987b3527e4db2389a1aba21af6015f736e19f7c6c2c25c.png] 

**Given:**

Total distance of the race = 900 m

In Case 1, Atul gives Vishu a head-start of 20 seconds and beats him by 135 m.

In Case 2, Atul gives Vishu a start of 189 m and beats him by 8 seconds.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let Atul's speed be vₐ and the time taken by Atul to cover 900 m be T seconds.

Let Vishu's speed be vv.

**Case 1:** Vishu runs for (T + 20) seconds but falls short by 135 m.

⇒ Distance covered by Vishu = 900 − 135 = 765 m

⇒ Time taken to cover 765 m = T + 20

⇒ 765 ÷ vv = T + 20 --- (Equation 1)

**Case 2:** Vishu gets a 189 m distance start, so he only needs to run 900 − 189 = 711 m.

Atul finishes in T seconds, but beats Vishu by 8 seconds.

⇒ Time taken by Vishu to cover 711 m = T + 8

⇒ 711 ÷ vv = T + 8 --- (Equation 2)

Subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ (765 ÷ vv) − (711 ÷ vv) = (T + 20) − (T + 8)

⇒ (765 − 711) ÷ vv = 12

⇒ 54 ÷ vv = 12

⇒ vv = 54 ÷ 12 = 4.5 m/s

Time taken by Vishu to complete the full 900 m race:

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 900 ÷ 4.5

⇒ Time = 200 seconds

⇒ 200 seconds = 3 minutes 20 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Head-start in Distance

When runner A gives B a start of x meters in a race of L meters, A covers the full L meters while B covers (L − x) meters.

Head-start in Time

When runner A gives B a head-start of t seconds, B begins running t seconds before A starts the race.

Beating by Distance or Time

If A beats B by x meters, B is x meters behind when A finishes. If A beats B by t seconds, B reaches the finish line t seconds after A.

questions.question: In a division problem, the divisor is 4 times the quotient and 2 times the remainder. If the remainder is 32, then find the dividend.

Remainder = 32

Divisor = 2 × 32 = 64

Quotient = 64 ÷ 4 = 16

Dividend = (64 × 16) + 32 = 1024 + 32 = 1056

**∴ The correct answer is 1056.**

Remainder = 32

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

⇒ 4 × Quotient = 64

⇒ Quotient = 64 ÷ 4 = 16

⇒ Dividend = (64 × 16) + 32

⇒ Dividend = 1024 + 32

⇒ Dividend = 1056

**∴ The correct answer is 1056.**

Division Algorithm

The core theorem states that Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder, where the remainder must always be greater than or equal to 0 and strictly less than the divisor.

Number of Divisors

For any integer represented in its prime factorization form as N = pa × qb × rc, the total number of divisors is given by (a + 1) × (b + 1) × (c + 1).

Divisibility Rules

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4, and it is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated uniformly on the original principal amount. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount A at the end of the given time period is the sum of the initial principal and the generated simple interest. Formula: A = P + SI = P × (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

Any point equidistant from vertices A and C (OA = OC) must lie on the perpendicular bisector of AC.

Hence, the interior point O must exclusively lie on the diagonal segment BD.

This makes D, O, and B collinear, forming a straight angle ∠DOB = 180º.

ABCD is a rhombus.

⇒ In rhombus ABCD, the diagonal BD functions strictly as the perpendicular bisector of the diagonal AC.

⇒ Because OA = OC, the interior point O is geometrically bounded to lie on this specific perpendicular bisector.

⇒ Consequently, O must lie on the interior line segment connecting points B and D.

⇒ With O positioned directly between B and D, the points D, O, and B become entirely collinear.

⇒ A collinear line visually forms a completely straight angle, meaning ∠DOB = 180º.

The bar graph below shows the production of coffee (in lakh tons) by four companies A, B, C and D over a period of four years from 2010 to 2013. Study the graph and answer the question that follows.

The combined average production for four years of companies A and C is what percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) more/less than the combined average production for four years of companies B and D?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/139e7f557467867c8b40e7f3acd9a006f6126f0c5ce59a20aaa7dbcd14b33aac.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The bar graph below shows the production of coffee (in lakh tons) by four companies A, B, C and D over a period of four years from 2010 to 2013. 

**Formula used:**

Combined average = (Sum of all values in Group 1 + Sum of all values in Group 2) / (Total number of values in both groups)

Percentage = (quantity1/quantity2) × 100 

**Calculation:**

The total production of coffee (in lakh tons) by company A over the period of four years = 60 + 90 + 140 + 220 = 510

The total production of coffee (in lakh tons) by company B over the period of four years = 70 + 100 + 150 + 210 = 530

The total production of coffee (in lakh tons) by company C over the period of four years = 50 + 190 + 180 + 250 = 670

The total production of coffee (in lakh tons) by company D over the period of four years = 120 + 170 + 200 + 260 = 750

Now,

The combined average production for four years of companies A and C is:

= (510 + 670)/8 = 147.5

The combined average production for four years of companies B and D is:

= (530 + 750)/8 = 160

Required percentage:

= [(160 - 147.5)/160] × 100

= 12.5/160 × 100

= 7.81% less

Hence, The combined average production for four years of companies A and C is 7.81% percentage less than the combined average production for four years of companies B and D.

**The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question:
Solve the given set of three equations to get the value of the unknowns:

x + 2z = 3

x + 2y + 3z = 5

3x - 5z = -13
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Solve equations (1) and (3) directly since they contain only variables x and z.

Multiply equation (1) by 3 to get: 3x + 6z = 9.

Subtract equation (3) from this: (3x + 6z) − (3x − 5z) = 9 − (−13) ⇒ 11z = 22 ⇒ z = 2.

Substitute z = 2 into equation (1): x + 4 = 3 ⇒ x = −1.

Substitute x = −1 and z = 2 into equation (2): −1 + 2y + 6 = 5 ⇒ 2y = 0 ⇒ y = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is x = −1, y = 0, z = 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 2z = 3 ... (i)

x + 2y + 3z = 5 ... (ii)

3x − 5z = −13 ... (iii)

**Calculation:**

⇒ From equation (i), we can express x in terms of z:

⇒ x = 3 − 2z ... (iv)

⇒ Substitute equation (iv) into equation (iii):

⇒ 3(3 − 2z) − 5z = −13

⇒ 9 − 6z − 5z = −13

⇒ 9 − 11z = −13

⇒ −11z = −13 − 9

⇒ −11z = −22

⇒ z = 2

⇒ Now, substitute z = 2 back into equation (iv):

⇒ x = 3 − 2(2)

⇒ x = 3 − 4 = −1

⇒ Finally, substitute x = −1 and z = 2 into equation (ii) to find y:

⇒ (−1) + 2y + 3(2) = 5

⇒ −1 + 2y + 6 = 5

⇒ 2y + 5 = 5

⇒ 2y = 0

⇒ y = 0

**∴ The correct answer is x = −1, y = 0, z = 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Three Variables

A system of three linear equations can have a unique solution, infinite solutions, or no solution depending on the determinants formed by their coefficients.

Substitution Method

This method involves expressing one variable in terms of the others from one equation and substituting it into the remaining equations to reduce the number of variables.

Elimination Method

By multiplying equations with suitable constants and adding or subtracting them, we can eliminate variables step-by-step to efficiently solve the system of equations.
</p

Effective Discount Formula

When two successive discounts of A% and B% are given, the equivalent single discount can be directly determined using: D = (A + B − A×B/100)%.

Relation between MP, CP, Profit%, and Discount%

The exact ratio of Marked Price (MP) to Cost Price (CP) when a certain profit is made after giving a discount is: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Buy X Get Y Free Discount

In scenarios involving free items, the net percentage discount is computed as: Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.
